title: They Work, but Try to Protect from the Sun
text:
They Work, but Try to Protect from the Sun. My patio has several type of furniture, one of which is a carry over from my previous home of 2 years ago. The furniture that was brought with me from old home is my glass table, patio chairs, and umbrella set. The furniture itself has stood the test of time, but the cushions, well, I have had to replace them for various reasons. And one set that I purchased for a quick replacement is Pillow Perfect Rounded Outdoor Chair Cushions.

I wanted cushions with a blue color scheme and that is what convinced me to buy these. The size was right and the price was right, so I went ahead and made the purchase. Attaching the cushions to my patio chairs was simple enough and required simply tying the strings on the back of the cushion, to secure them to the chair.

The comfort level of these cushions is certainly good. They are thick and I can sit on them for a while and still feel comfy. This is certainly important, but there are two concerns I have with these cushions that could influence if I buy them again: The tendency to fade and the tendency of the strings to break off. The fading is due, of course, to exposure to the sun and because of where my table and chairs are situated, they are exposed to a good deal of sunshine. This has caused the colors to noticeably fade, even after a single summer season. If possible, it is a good idea to keep your cushions in a shaded space or remove them during the colder season and store in a safe, dry, unsunny place.

Then, there is the tendency of the strings on the back- the ones you use to tie the cushions to the chairs- the break off. When this happens, there is no easy way to fix. I have found that, as long as only one string breaks, I'm usually fine because the other will hold the cushion in place. If two break, well, your cushion may very well start to flop in the wind. It really depends on how often you use the cushions. If you sit in them and move around a lot, like we do, then eventually, the strings are going to break.

Chair cushions are necessary when you on a patio set like mine and these cushions are fine for occasional use. Like I said, you can extend the life of the cushions and prevent fading by keeping out of the sun, but the issue with fading and the tendency of the strings to break off convince me to lower my rating to average overall.
